standard.title: Glossary of Terms Relating to River Valley Projects — Part 11 Hydrology, Section 1 General Terms (First Revision)
standard.sector: Water Resources Department / Hydrology and Water Resources Management
standard.description: This standard specifies standard terminology and precise definitions relating to hydrology, specifically general hydrological terms, to prevent ambiguity in their interpretation and ensure uniform communication across river valley development, irrigation systems, and water resources planning projects in India.
standard.scope: This standard specifies standard terminology and precise definitions relating to hydrology, specifically general hydrological terms, to prevent ambiguity in their interpretation and ensure uniform communication across river valley development, irrigation systems, and water resources planning projects in India.

version.current_version: First Revision, November 2024 (established by the Water Resources Department of BIS to modernize and replace the legacy 1972 first edition)

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this newly established 2024 revision (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Terminology Code. Since IS 4410 (Part 11/Sec 1) is an operational glossary defining standardized technical terms rather than a manufactured physical material, it does not carry an individual BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its standardized definitions (such as 'Water Year' boundaries, 'Thermograph' specifications, and hydrological definitions) is universally mandated in public river valley contracts, Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), hydrological study submissions to the Central Water Commission (CWC), and academic research across India to ensure technical precision, prevent contractual ambiguity, and establish clean engineering baselines.
requirements: Standardises the term for a stream of water flowing with great velocity or turbulence, specifically during a freshet or down a steep incline, to establish uniform hydraulic classifications.
Defines a thermograph as an instrument designed for the automatic recording of temperatures, providing a standard reference term for hydrological monitoring facilities.

Standardises a water year as a continuous twelve-month period selected for maintaining or presenting records of flow, and/or use of water or any river system, enabling uniform annual reporting boundaries.
Mandates that water resources, irrigation, and river valley planning terminology be integrated with the broader multi-part IS 4410 series, including Part 1 (Irrigation Practice).
Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing temperature, period, or flow metrics must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with standard rules to determine code compliance.
